title: Interactive patterns: scenarios for small screens and data-dense views
creator: Priya Singh
description: Create a focused documentation update that captures pragmatic usage patterns for interactive components when used on small screens and in data-dense contexts. This ticket covers: responsive token guidance (spacing, typography scale for dense lists), compact button variants and touch target trade-offs, condensed table layouts and row-level affordances, and chart micro-interactions (tooltips, axis labels) for narrow viewports. Deliverables: updated docsite pages, code examples (React), migration notes for token renames, and a lightweight cookbook of do/don't scenarios.
acceptance_criteria: New doc pages published to docs-2026.03 with the small-screen/data-dense guidance section
At least 6 concrete code examples (JSX) demonstrating tokens -> compact variants for buttons, tables, and charts
Migration notes clarify mapping for at least 8 tokens and include an automated codemod suggestion link
Design review sign-off and one engineering review comment thread resolved
Smoke test: examples render correctly in Chrome/Firefox mobile emulation and on an iPhone 12 snapshot
design_notes: Principle: prioritize clarity over parity — components can deviate from default spacing to preserve information density.
Spacing guidance: introduce a small-dense spacing scale (space-2 / 4px, space-4 / 8px) derived from existing tokens instead of ad-hoc hardcoded values.

Buttons: create 'compact' touch-aware variants. Minimum tappable size for touch is 40px but allow visually smaller buttons (32px) when a tooltip or primary action is present; provide explicit a11y note.
Tables: prefer condensed row height + horizontal scrolling for many columns rather than truncating important fields; show examples with sticky first column and inline ellipsis with popover on tap.
Charts: avoid cramped axis labels — prefer simplified tick sets and on-demand detail in tooltips or an accessible data table alternative.
migration_notes:
TOKEN_MAPPINGS:
- legacy-spacing-xs -> token-space-2 (4px)
- legacy-spacing-s -> token-space-4 (8px)
- text-sm-condensed -> type-scale-12-condensed
- btn-height-sm -> button-height-compact (32px)
- table-row-height-default -> table-row-height-dense (36px)
Codemod suggestion: link to example codemod in repo to rename spacing tokens: https://github.com/redwood-inference/codemods/rename-space-tokens
Migration strategy: provide wrapper CSS classes (.rwd-compact) to opt-in per route before full token swap; include QA checklist for visual diffs (Percy) and RTL verification.
Edge cases: components that depend on fixed internal paddings (legacy third-party tables) will need shallow adaptors; list included in known-legacy-components.md link.
examples:
// Chart micro-interaction pattern
<LineChart compact axes="minimal" onPointTap={openDataTooltip} />

// CSS token usage
.container { padding: var(--token-space-2); font-size: var(--type-12-condensed); }
do_and_dont: DO: Use compact variants for secondary actions when screen width < 480px.
DO: Provide an accessible reveal for truncated table cell content (popover or inline expansion).
DON'T: Reduce font size below the condensed type-scale for body copy — prefer layout adjustments instead.
DON'T: Use absolute pixel paddings sprinkled in components; rely on tokens and the compact scale.
DO: Add visual tests for each example to catch regression in density behavior.
